key_insight: RheOFormer’s failures in viscoplastic flow prediction can be mitigated with logarithmic velocity representations, gradient-aware losses, and a few strategically selected training cases.
engineering_relevance: These remedies support more data-efficient CFD surrogates for yield-stress fluids, particularly in low-gradient plug regions and underrepresented flow regimes.
method: Evaluate RheOFormer on steady Bingham channel flow across dataset structures, value ranges, and input representations.
Use logarithmic velocity representations and gradient-aware losses to improve plug-region predictions.
Add a few cases covering missing physical regimes to reduce extrapolation errors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved accuracy in challenging regimes, reduced extrapolation errors, and accurate steady-state prediction from one partially developed snapshot, outperforming input copying.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to a simple channel geometry and Bingham constitutive model; transfer to complex geometries or other rheologies remains unestablished.
paper_title: Failure Modes and Data-Efficient Remedies for Transformer-Based Prediction of Viscoplastic Flows
